newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa, United extend joint cargo sales test.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa, United extend joint cargo sales test.

text.p: United Airlines and Lufthansa Cargo have extended their joint cargo sales pilot project until the end of November, United's cargo sales manager, Robert Blythe, said.
The two airline have added an extra month to the joint sales tests in Paris and San Francisco because of delays at Charles de Gaulle airport, he explained.
Lufthansa said on October 18 it would start joint cargo capacity selling in Europe with United Airlines from November at agreed joint rates following the trial period.
"We are extending the trial period up to the end of November. October was a very tight timeframe so we decided to extend it," Blythe told Reuters.
Additional security rules at Charles de Gaulle airport forced all cargo destined for the U.S. to be held 24 hours for checks during October, he explained.
This rule affected all airlines except for Federal Express which as a freight-only airline carried no passengers, he noted.
Now the 24-hour rule had been lifted Lufthansa and United were in a better position to market joint cargo sales, he said.

Under their anti-trust immunity status, the airlines plan to develop a global cargo partnership covering joint sales and marketing and timetable co-ordination to build a worldwide air cargo network. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
